To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DNA extracted from phenolic rich bark samples of four Terminalia species can be used for PCR amplification after removal of the secondary metabolite phenolics by a simple method of dilution and heat treatment.
the DNA quality and PCR amplification of phenolic rich barks can be improved by using customized solutions for the DNA extraction and PCR optimization.
the DNA from the phenolic rich barks of Terminalia species can be successfully amplified using homogenous PCR after the removal of the phenolics and hard tissues by the customized solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient and cost effective protocol for PCR based detection of Terminalia species adulteration in commercial herbal preparations.
the development of DNA-based analytical methods and the improvement of their applicability for quality control and standardization of herbal drugs.
development of a simple, rapid, sensitive and cost effective method for the analysis of the Terminalia species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DNA from the phenolic rich bark can be used for PCR amplification after a simple and economic treatment.
the phenolic rich barks of the four species of Terminalia can be successfully amplified using homogenous PCR method.
DNA from phenolic rich tissue of Terminalia species could be used as template for PCR based analysis after a simple and economic protocol.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quality of the DNA obtained from the bark tissue can be improved by simple methods of DNA extraction and PCR amplification.
the DNA quality parameters and its PCR amplifiability is not directly proportional to phenolic content.
the quality of DNA is not only dependent on the amount of the starting material and the extraction procedure, but also on the presence of secondary metabolites like polyphenols in the sample.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the DNA from the phenolic rich barks of Terminalia species can be used for PCR amplification of the target DNA after the removal of phenolics by simple and cost effective methods like dilution and heat denaturation.
DNA from the hard and phenol rich bark tissue can be successfully used for PCR amplification of the genomic DNA by following a comprehensive strategy.
the DNA quality can be improved by simple and inexpensive methods like phenolic removal, DNA precipitation and dilution of crude extract.
